channel.title: NewsCenter — All newsletter news — 2026-11-07
channel.description: Every news received through Laurent's newsletters over the last 24 hours. 54 news received.

item.title: The iPhone Duo surpasses 100,000 optimized apps
item.description: Apple says the iPhone Duo now has more than 100,000 apps adapted to its foldable display, with thousands of new apps added every day. Microsoft Word, Outlook, Zoom, Etsy, Goodnotes, and sports apps have recently joined the list.

item.title: OpenAI reportedly raises an additional $11 billion
item.description: OpenAI has reportedly raised an additional $11 billion, at a valuation of $1.25 trillion.

item.title: AST SpaceMobile wants to build its own rockets to catch up with Starlink Mobile
item.description: AST SpaceMobile plans to build its own rockets in order to catch up with Starlink Mobile.

item.title: Elon Musk says government contracts will account for less than 10% of SpaceX revenue
item.description: Elon Musk says government activities will account for less than 10% of SpaceX’s revenue.

item.title: Lawsuit claims a woman used ChatGPT to plan her husband’s murder
item.description: According to a lawsuit, a man introduced his wife to ChatGPT, after which she allegedly used the service to plan his murder.

item.title: BET president uses AI with constant human oversight
item.description: Louis Carr says he regularly tests ChatGPT, Claude, and other AI tools while emphasizing the need for a human editor. BET has used AI, among other things, to arrange seating and verify tributes at the BET Awards.

item.title: Early reviews praise the MacBook Pro PROLED’s display
item.description: Early reviews of the MacBook Pro PROLED praise its display but criticize its price and pay little attention to the touchscreen.

item.title: Early deliveries reveal Apple’s new Macs
item.description: The first iPad mini, MacBook Pro and iMac units began shipping to customers on Friday, offering a closer look at the devices.

item.title: iPhone 20 could drop the Action button
item.description: According to a source with a mixed track record, the iPhone 20 lineup could drop the Action button.

item.title: iPhone 18e is not expected to receive a major redesign
item.description: A Weibo leaker claims that the iPhone 18e will not receive any significant design changes.

item.title: iPhone 18 could have a larger battery and cost more
item.description: According to another source, the standard iPhone 18 would have a larger battery and a higher price.

item.title: Siri handles more than 2.5 billion requests every day
item.description: Siri receives more than 2.5 billion daily requests, putting Apple’s AI overhaul into perspective.

item.title: Apple still cannot meet demand for iPhone Duo
item.description: Apple cannot meet demand for iPhone Duo, while Mac and iPad supplies will remain limited through the end of 2026.

item.title: Mac and iPad supplies will remain limited through the end of 2026
item.description: Apple expects supply constraints for Macs and iPads at least through the end of 2026.

item.title: AI solves an 18-year-old quantum computing puzzle
item.description: Research company PSI says it solved the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture using an automated system that produced a proof accepted by Lean in three days. The result has not yet undergone a full independent academic review.

item.title: Amazon lets some customers shop by text with Alexa
item.description: Amazon is allowing a small group of invited U.S. customers to text its Alexa for Shopping agent to search for products, place orders, and track prices. Access is expected to expand to millions of people in the coming weeks.

item.title: Fox finalizes $22 billion acquisition of Roku
item.description: Fox has completed its $22 billion acquisition of Roku, strengthening its position in streaming and connected TV. The deal gives Fox direct access to more than 100 million households and is expected to improve ad targeting.

item.title: Microsoft ends its AI cloud contract with Oracle
item.description: Microsoft will not renew the 2023 contract to rent AI computing power from Oracle, partly because the hardware relied on older Nvidia chips. Oracle nevertheless says demand for its AI infrastructure, including older GPUs, remains strong.

item.title: AMD now defines itself as a data center-focused company
item.description: CEO Lisa Su says server chips now define AMD, with the data center segment accounting for about 63% of third-quarter 2026 revenue. Quarterly revenue reached $13.4 billion, while gaming sales fell 40%.

item.title: U.S. indicts three men in CEO voice scam
item.description: Three men are facing charges in the United States over a $129 million fraud that allegedly used AI to imitate the voices of corporate executives.

item.title: Six pallets of Nvidia GPUs worth $11.4 million stolen
item.description: Six pallets of Nvidia GPUs valued at $11.4 million were stolen during a cargo burglary in California.

item.title: Online magazine Salon announces its closure
item.description: Online magazine Salon, one of the earliest iconic media outlets associated with internet discussions, says it will shut down.

item.title: First 200 mm single-crystal diamond produced in the United States
item.description: The first 200 mm single-crystal diamond was grown in the United States. It could help advance next-generation chip development.

item.title: Google DeepMind agents expose weaknesses in old encryption
item.description: Google DeepMind agents have exposed weaknesses in older encryption methods, with a claimed speed 1,600 times faster.

item.title: Meta launches Spaces for collaboration with its Muse agent
item.description: Meta is introducing Spaces, a new way to collaborate with its Muse agent.

item.title: Alphabet reveals a $548 million stake in Qualcomm
item.description: Alphabet disclosed that it holds a $548 million stake in chipmaker Qualcomm.

item.title: AI teddy bear for children produced a self-harm response
item.description: The BBC found that an AI-equipped teddy bear intended for three-year-old children spontaneously gave a response related to self-harm.

item.title: Crusoe resells struggling Wyoming data center project to Google
item.description: Crusoe is selling Google a troubled data center project in Wyoming.

item.title: Chainalysis says hackers stole the credentials of all its customers
item.description: Chainalysis says hackers stole the credentials and access tokens of all its customers.

item.title: TSMC considers entering AI memory chips at Nvidia’s request
item.description: TSMC is considering entering the market for AI memory chips at Nvidia’s request.

item.title: What is known about the victims of the Learjet crash
item.description: Adam Robinson, founder of a technology company in Austin, died with his wife Helen Sharp, their children, their friends Rachel Reed and Charmi Fehr, and their nanny Ana María Ramírez Cetina when their private jet crashed in Florida.

item.title: MIT teaches robots to correct false memories
item.description: MIT researchers developed a system that flags uncertain descriptions of objects, compares images taken from different angles, and corrects a robot’s memory errors. In tests, it resolved ambiguities involving about 92% of objects in the environment.

item.title: Waymo will end its exclusive agreement with Uber
item.description: Waymo plans to let passengers in Austin and Atlanta book rides directly through its own app starting in January 2028. The company says its customers want a more consistent experience and a direct relationship with Waymo.

item.title: Agility Robotics finalizes merger and prepares for Nasdaq listing
item.description: Agility Robotics has finalized its merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI. The deal paves the way for the maker of Digit to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker AGLT.

item.title: Tutor Intelligence raises $75 million to expand its robot fleet
item.description: Tutor Intelligence raised $75 million in a round led by Andreessen Horowitz. The company wants to expand its robot fleet, which learns from real-world industrial assignments with help from remote human operators.

item.title: RoboScience raises several hundred million yuan
item.description: Beijing-based RoboScience has reportedly completed a new funding round worth several hundred million yuan. The company wants to develop its robotic AI and expand trials in logistics, retail, and industry.

item.title: Curbie automates taking out the trash
item.description: Revere Robotics is developing Curbie, a small robot that attaches to an ordinary trash bin, takes it to the curb, and returns it after collection. The robot is still being field-tested, with no price or launch date announced.

item.title: Frequent traveler reveals her method for choosing the best seat
item.description: A frequent traveler shares her strategy for choosing the best seat on a plane and traveling more comfortably, even in economy class.

item.title: Dermatologists recommend washing your face less often
item.description: According to dermatologist Ariel Ostad, rinsing your face with water is often enough. Harsh scrubs can damage the skin’s natural protective barrier.

item.title: John Turturro looks back on his most memorable roles
item.description: John Turturro, who has more than 100 film and television roles, discusses his collaborations with Spike Lee and the Coen brothers, as well as several memorable roles from his career.

item.title: Flight attendant prefers keeping airplane window shades open
item.description: Leanna Coy believes open shades allow passengers to enjoy the view and better see the outside environment, which reassures her. She notes, however, that the decision is not hers to make.

item.title: Joe Manganiello reveals his habits for staying healthy
item.description: After suffering from chronic autoimmune problems for seven years, Joe Manganiello describes his health habits, including testosterone-free workouts and flotation sessions.

item.title: Apple envisions smart locks with adaptive unlocking
item.description: An Apple patent describes locks that can automatically unlock based on the user’s approach.

item.title: A nine-inch HomeView Ultra is expected in 2027 or 2028
item.description: Apple could launch a nine-inch HomeView Ultra in 2027 or 2028.

item.title: Apple beats forecasts with record quarterly results
item.description: Apple generated 114.5 billion dollars in revenue in the fourth quarter of 2026, beating Wall Street forecasts and its previous quarterly record from the 2020 holiday season.

item.title: Rising memory costs weigh on Apple’s results
item.description: Apple warned that an imminent increase in memory prices could drive up the cost of its products.

item.title: Apple must disclose details of its donation to Trump’s ballroom
item.description: Apple reportedly donated 25 million dollars to Donald Trump’s White House ballroom project. A Senate subcommittee is now requesting documents related to the donation.

item.title: Rave’s lawsuit against Apple is transferred to California
item.description: Rave’s lawsuit against Apple, which accuses the company of copying SharePlay features and removing Rave from the App Store, has been transferred to California.

item.title: Supreme Court to hear Apple v. Epic case in January 2027
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court will hear arguments in the case between Epic Games and Apple in January 2027.

item.title: HomePod mini 2 slightly improves sound and connectivity
item.description: The HomePod mini 2 offers slightly better sound and expanded connectivity, but costs 50 dollars more than the original model and may not justify an upgrade.

item.title: Siri Recaps and Live Rewind deemed controversial and of little use
item.description: After testing, Siri Recaps and Live Rewind are described as controversial and useless technologies, despite Apple’s usual privacy and security measures.

item.title: Walmart wants AI assistants to shop for you
item.description: Last month, Walmart announced that AI assistants will be able to shop for you, with spending limits and approvals that you define. AI is thus moving from answering questions to carrying out tasks.

item.title: A prompt for controlling actions performed by AI
item.description: Instead of asking AI to freely process an inbox, have it list every action and classify it as READ, DRAFT or ACT. AI can perform reading and preparation steps, but must stop and request confirmation before any action that sends, publishes, pays, deletes or changes something.

item.title: AI Bootcamp: applying a rule to secure AI actions
item.description: The chapter explains how to turn advice into actions, choose tasks based on the cost of failure, and distinguish a bad answer from a bad action. It also shows how to prevent a hostile page from transmitting its instructions to the assistant.
